setting.language.label: Language
setting.language.help: The language of the launcher. Auto follows your Windows language (Portuguese (Brazil) or English); the other two choices always use that language.
setting.renderer.label: Renderer
setting.renderer.help: GSdx (ARMSX2) runs the ARMSX2 emulator's GS inside the game and is the default of this private build. CoreGS 2.0 is our own renderer and the second choice, with a much lower processor cost.
setting.vsync.help_coregs20: On keeps motion smooth with no tearing. Off lowers latency and may tear.
settings.gsdx_text: GSdx is not on this PC yet. It is an optional renderer, downloaded from the internet. If you cancel, CoreGS 2.0 stays selected.
settings.gsdx_file_hint: On another network or PC, download the newest gt4-gs-…-windows-x64.zip from github.com/moesuito/gt4recomp-gs/releases, then pick it here.
setting.frame_rate.label: Frame rate (experimental)
setting.frame_rate.help: 60 FPS is the default: in a race, when the PC cannot keep up, the frame rate drops instead of the game slowing down, with the same physics. The 30 FPS mode is for weaker PCs: races draw 30 frames per second. Both are experimental; menus stay at 60.
setting.present_thread.label: Presentation thread (one-queue GPUs)
setting.present_thread.help: For the Steam Deck and other graphics cards that have a single queue for graphics work. The game shows finished frames from a separate thread, so it does not wait for the screen. On other graphics cards this changes nothing: they already do it.
setting.coregs_sharpening.label: Sharpening (FSR1)
setting.coregs_sharpening.help: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 sharpening of the final picture. Off leaves the picture as the game drew it.
setting.texture_load.label: Load custom textures
setting.texture_load.help: Loads the texture pack from the Textures folder: put the pack's files straight in it. An empty folder changes nothing.
setting.graphics_api.label: API
setting.graphics_api.help: Automatic uses Vulkan when the graphics card supports Vulkan 1.2, otherwise Direct3D 11. Choose Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Direct3D 11 to force one.
setting.graphics_card.label: Graphics card
setting.graphics_card.help: The graphics card that draws the game. Automatic picks a dedicated card over integrated graphics, then the one with the most video memory.
setting.render_scale.label: Render scale
setting.render_scale.help: How sharp the picture is drawn. 100% is the automatic scale that covers your screen (taken from the Resolution setting on the Display page); below that it is faster and softer, above it is sharper and needs a much faster GPU. The size next to the control is the 16:9 picture of the resulting internal resolution.
setting.armsx2_api.label: ARMSX2 GS graphics API
setting.armsx2_api.help: Auto leaves the graphics API to the ARMSX2 GS itself (Vulkan when this build carries it, OpenGL ES otherwise), so its per-GPU rules stay in charge. Vulkan is experimental: ARMSX2 keeps it out of its Android renderer choice because of blending bugs, and this build may not carry it at all (the game log then says so and stays on OpenGL ES).
setting.armsx2_fxaa.label: Anti-aliasing (FXAA)
setting.armsx2_fxaa.help: Fast approximate anti-aliasing applied to the finished picture by the ARMSX2 GS. Off by default: it costs a little graphics time and softens the image slightly.
setting.armsx2_cas.label: Sharpening (CAS)
setting.armsx2_cas.help: Contrast adaptive sharpening of the finished picture, the ARMSX2 GS's own sharpening filter. Off by default.
setting.armsx2_cas_strength.label: Sharpening amount
setting.armsx2_cas_strength.help: Strength of the ARMSX2 GS sharpening (0 to 100). Used when sharpening is on.
setting.armsx2_filter.label: Texture filtering
setting.armsx2_filter.help: How the ARMSX2 GS samples game textures. Bilinear (PS2) follows the console; Nearest is the sharpest and the most aliased; the forced modes override what the game asks for.
setting.armsx2_aniso.label: Anisotropic filtering
setting.armsx2_aniso.help: Anisotropic filtering of the ARMSX2 GS. Off keeps the frame time budget; 16x is the sharpest and costs graphics time.
setting.armsx2_dither.label: Dithering
setting.armsx2_dither.help: The dithering the ARMSX2 GS applies. PS2 (unscaled) is the console's own, which is what the original picture has; Off shows the bands the dithering hides; Scaled grows it with the resolution.
setting.monitor.label: Monitor
setting.monitor.help: The screen the game opens on. The primary monitor is used until you pick another one.
setting.resolution.label: Resolution
setting.resolution.help: The size of the picture, from the sizes your monitor supports. The shape of the screen follows it: at 16:9 the game is unchanged, other shapes widen or heighten the race view. A size below the monitor's own is drawn at that size and stretched to fill the screen.
setting.fullscreen.label: Fullscreen
setting.fullscreen.help: Start in fullscreen on the chosen monitor (a borderless window that covers it). Alt+Enter or F11 switches while playing.
setting.vsync.label: VSync
setting.vsync.help: On keeps motion smooth with no tearing. Fast and Off lower latency and may tear. Modes the graphics driver lacks are not offered.
setting.performance_hud.label: Performance HUD
setting.performance_hud.help: Shows a panel in the corner while you play. FPS only shows just the frame rate. Full shows the names of your graphics card and processor, the frame rate and frame time with a live graph, the game's use of the processor, the graphics card and memory, and the state of the performance report when that is turned on.
setting.performance_report.label: Performance report
setting.performance_report.help: Records frame timing while you play for bug reports.
setting.discord_rich_presence.label: Discord Rich Presence
setting.discord_rich_presence.help: Shows that you are playing Gran Turismo 4 or Gran Turismo 4 Spec II in your Discord profile while a game runs. Shows the game name, GT4Recomp and the session time. No mode, track, car, save, account or path is shared. On by default; turn it off to keep your play private.
setting.check_vu_code.label: Check compiled VU code
setting.check_vu_code.help: Compares compiled vector-unit code with the reference while playing. Slower.
setting.l2_deadzone.label: L2 deadzone
setting.r2_deadzone.label: R2 deadzone
setting.l2_curve.label: L2 curve
setting.r2_curve.label: R2 curve
setting.lstick_deadzone.label: Left stick deadzone
setting.rstick_deadzone.label: Right stick deadzone
setting.trigger_deadzone.help: How far the trigger must travel before it counts, in percent of its travel. The pressure the game reads starts above this point.
setting.trigger_curve.help: How the pressure grows with the trigger travel. Linear follows the trigger; quadratic and cubic give finer control at light pressure.
setting.stick_deadzone.help: How far the stick must move from the centre before the game sees it, in percent of its travel. The default is the XInput standard; lower it for a precise pad, raise it for one that drifts.

setting.trigger_full_range.label: Full trigger range
setting.trigger_full_range.help: Throttle and brake follow the whole travel of the triggers in finer steps: about 255 levels instead of the game's own 46 for the throttle and 85 for the brake, still 100% at the end of the travel. Off is the game as it was made.
controls.meter_help: Grey: the trigger now. Blue: the pressure the game reads. Stripes: the deadzone.

controls.capture_foot: B cancels, so it cannot be picked here. To move B, rebind the button that has it and choose Swap.

setting.blending.label: Blending accuracy
setting.blending.help: How exactly the graphics card combines colours when the game blends two layers. High is exact and is the default. Minimum is faster (the old Performance Mode used it, about 1.5 ms less per frame on the weak laptop) and can make some translucent effects look wrong.
setting.hw_download_mode.label: Readbacks
setting.hw_download_mode.help: How the graphics plugin reads images back from the graphics card. Accurate (default) is exact. Any other value is faster but the car icons next to the gap time can come out blank and the loading screen picture may be missing.
setting.effect_flares.label: Sun glare and light flares
setting.effect_flares.help: The sun's glare and the night lights' flares. Turning them off is the biggest speed gain of the old Performance Mode: the game no longer reads the flare visibility table back from the graphics card every frame, so the processor never waits for it.
setting.effect_road_sheen.label: Road sheen
setting.effect_road_sheen.help: The shine over the road that GT4 draws as a full-screen pass. Turning it off removes a whole-screen pass every frame in a race; the road looks duller and a little darker.
setting.effect_targets.label: Small effects
setting.effect_targets.help: The resolution of the small effect pictures GT4 draws inside a scaled frame (glow, reflections). Full resolution is exact and is the default. Lower draws them at 1x, the old Performance Mode's choice: faster, and small effects look softer.
setting.fxaa.label: Anti-aliasing
setting.fxaa.help: Smooths jagged edges with a fast filter. It softens fine detail a little. Off by default.
setting.cas_mode.label: Sharpening (CAS)
setting.cas_mode.help: FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening. Off leaves the picture as the game drew it.
setting.cas_sharpness.label: Sharpening amount
setting.cas_sharpness.help: How strong the CAS sharpening is. Used when CAS is on.
setting.perf_overlay.label: Performance overlay
setting.perf_overlay.help: Shows GT4Recomp's own overlay while you play (FPS, frame time, CPU and GPU use).
setting.perf_overlay_fps.label: Overlay: FPS
setting.perf_overlay_fps.help: Shows the frame rate in the performance overlay.
setting.launcher_gpu.label: Launcher GPU acceleration
setting.launcher_gpu.help: Off keeps the launcher window without GPU acceleration, after it failed to draw in WebView2. On takes effect at the next start of the launcher.
rust.saves.went_to_game: It went to {game}, the game this save belongs to.
about.logs_exported_text: The log bundle is saved as {path}. Attach that zip to a GitHub issue.
logs.offer_title: The game stopped with an error
logs.offer_text: Export the logs and attach the zip to a GitHub issue, so the problem can be found.
rust.logs.export_title: Choose a folder for the log bundle
rust.logs.export_failed: The logs could not be exported: {error}
rust.textures.invalid_not_absolute: Choose a folder with a complete path, starting from a drive letter.
rust.textures.invalid_not_folder: That is a file, not a folder. Choose the folder that holds the textures.
rust.textures.invalid_data_root: That is the launcher's own data folder. Choose the folder that holds the textures instead.
rust.textures.invalid_renderer: That folder belongs to the renderer and is replaced when it updates. Choose another folder.
setting.update_channel.label: Channel
setting.update_channel.help: Stable gets the normal releases. Beta also gets the release candidates, to try new features early. Going back to Stable never installs an older version by itself.
versions.label: Version
versions.help: Pick the GT4Recomp version to install. The list is read from GitHub each time this page opens. Stable lists the normal releases; Beta lists the release candidates.
versions.older_note: Older versions are not listed: they cannot read this version's data.
versions.only_installed: There is no other version on this channel yet. Versions older than 1.3.0-rc5 are not listed: they cannot read this version's data.
versions.nothing_newer: You are on a newer version than any {channel} release; {channel} updates resume when a newer release ships.
versions.confirm_text: GT4Recomp downloads version {version}, checks it, installs it and closes. Start it again afterwards. Your settings and saves are kept.
versions.downgrade_text: You are on {installed}. Version {version} is older.
versions.downgrade_warning: Going back to an older version can break settings, saves or other data. Back up your saves first (Saves > Export, or the saves folder).
rust.update.versions_failed: Could not read the version list ({reason}). Your current version stays.
ra.title: Achievements
ra.subtitle: Sign in with your RetroAchievements account to unlock achievements in-game and record them on retroachievements.org.
ra.relogin_required_desc: Your saved session cannot be unlocked on this Windows account or PC. Sign in again to reconnect your account.
ra.migration_failed_desc: Your saved credentials could not be protected on this PC. Sign in again to save a protected session.
ra.save_failed_desc: Your RetroAchievements settings could not be saved to disk. Check file permissions or disk space.
ra.opt_enabled_help: Starts a RetroAchievements session when the game launches, evaluates PS2 memory triggers each frame, shows on-screen achievement popups, and submits unlocks to retroachievements.org.
ra.opt_hardcore_help: Earns Hardcore points and mastery badges on RetroAchievements.
ra.opt_encore_help: Allows achievements you have already unlocked to trigger again during this session.
ra.modal_text: Your password is sent once over HTTPS to retroachievements.org to obtain an API token. Only your username and protected token are stored on this PC.
ra.err_save_migration: Cannot change options: your existing login credentials could not be protected. Please sign in again.
ra.err_save_failed: Failed to save RetroAchievements settings. Check file permissions or disk space.
ra.sign_out_text: Your stored API token will be removed from this PC.
ra.unsupported_title: RetroAchievements is not available for Gran Turismo 4 Spec II
ra.unsupported_desc: Achievements are supported only on the original Gran Turismo 4 (v2.00) release. You can switch to Gran Turismo 4 in the Games menu to view and unlock achievements.
wheel.title: Racing wheel
wheel.tip: GT4 sees a Logitech Driving Force Pro: it uses its own wheel driver (900 degrees) and its own force feedback. Your wheel feeds it through wheel.toml in the GT4Recomp data folder.
wheel.enabled_help: On: GT4 finds a Driving Force Pro plugged in and plays its own force feedback on your wheel. Off: no wheel in the game.
wheel.panel_label: The wheel, the selected control and force feedback
wheel.no_wheel_text: Connect the wheel and turn it on. Many wheels also need their own software running (Logitech G HUB, Thrustmaster, Fanatec, MOZA Pit House...).
wheel.connect_hint: Connect it, or turn it on
wheel.status_other: Connected · not the wheel set up here
wheel.family_unknown: Not a known model: map it with Set up the wheel
wheel.ffb_line.yes: Force feedback: yes (Test force lists the effects)
wheel.set_900: Set the wheel to 900 degrees in {software}, and keep 900 here.
wheel.set_900_generic: Set the wheel to 900 degrees in its own software, and keep 900 here.
wheel.note.logitech_compatibility: If this is a G25, G27 or Driving Force GT, it is in compatibility mode (fewer buttons, no clutch). Open Logitech G HUB or Logitech Profiler and set native mode.
wheel.note.thrustmaster_initial: This Thrustmaster base is still in its start-up mode. Install or open the Thrustmaster drivers so it switches to its normal mode.
wheel.note.logitech_g920_initial: This G920 is still in its start-up mode. Open Logitech G HUB so it switches to its normal mode.
wheel.note.fanatec_console_mode: This Fanatec base is in console mode. Put it in PC mode (see the Fanatec manual).
wheel.note.no_force_feedback: This wheel has no force feedback.
wheel.configured_missing: The wheel set up here ({name}) is not connected.
wheel.drive_device_help: With several devices connected, the game reads its steering and buttons from this one. Pedals or a shifter on their own USB device keep working.
wheel.sub.steering: The game's 900 degrees, 1:1 with your wheel
wheel.sub.clutch: Shown here only: the Driving Force Pro has no clutch
wheel.sub.gear_up: Driving Force Pro R1 · right paddle
wheel.sub.gear_down: Driving Force Pro L1 · left paddle
wheel.click_again: Click the control again to bind it.
wheel.meter_help: Grey: the pedal now. Colour: what the game gets. Stripes: the dead zone. Line: full.
wheel.rotation_help: Your wheel's lock-to-lock range. GT4 turns its wheel 900 degrees: set 900 in the wheel's software and here, so the car's wheel turns exactly like yours.
wheel.rotation_warning: Not 900: the car steers differently from your wheel
wheel.steer_invert_help: Turn on if the car steers right when you turn left. Set up the wheel finds it for you.
wheel.pedal_mode_help: How the pedal reports its travel. Standard: it rests at the top of its axis (most wheels). Reversed: it rests at the bottom (many direct-drive and load-cell pedals). Half axis: it rests at the centre. Shared axis: the accelerator and the brake share one axis, each on one half. Set up the wheel finds it for you.
wheel.deadzone_help: The first part of the travel that does nothing, so a foot resting on the pedal does not press it.
wheel.saturation_help: How far the pedal goes before the game gets 100%. Lower it if your pedal never reaches the end.
wheel.curve_help: Linear follows the pedal directly; quadratic and cubic give finer control at the start of the travel.
wheel.ffb.title: Force feedback
wheel.ffb.enabled_help: The game's own forces (the self-aligning torque, the spring in the menus) played on your wheel.
wheel.ffb.strength_help: Scales the forces the game sends. Direct-drive bases are strong: start low and raise it.
wheel.ffb.damper_help: A little damping the wheel always has, even when the game sends none. It calms the wheel on fast straights.
wheel.ffb.invert_help: Turn on if the wheel pushes away from the centre in a race instead of pulling back to it.
wheel.ffb.test_help: The wheel pulls to one side, then to the other, for about a second. Hold it lightly.
wheel.ffb.test_no_ffb: {name} has no force feedback through SDL. {error}
wheel.ffb.test_no_constant: {name} could not play a constant force (effects: {effects}).
wheel.ffb.test_game: Close the game to test: the game owns the force feedback while it runs.
wheel.ffb.received: Force feedback in the last game
wheel.received_reason.summary: The game sent {commands} force commands and the wheel played them ({played} force updates; a newer force replaces an older one that was not sent yet).
wheel.received_reason.ended_early: The game ended before it could report it.
wheel.received_reason.no_haptics: The game found no force feedback on the wheel.
wheel.received_reason.no_wheel_file: The game found no wheel file.
wheel.received_reason.refused: The game refused the wheel file: {error}
wheel.received_reason.wheel_off: The wheel was off in that game.
wheel.received_reason.no_wheel_lines: That game build did not report it.
wheel.presets.title: Presets
wheel.presets.note: A preset keeps this mapping and force settings as a file, to load again or share.
wheel.presets.save_text: Presets are files in the launcher's config folder (wheel-presets), in the same format as wheel.toml.
wheel.presets.name: Preset name
wheel.presets.reset_text: Every binding and setting goes back to the defaults, and the wheel is turned off in the game.
wheel.presets.reset_done: The wheel settings are back to the defaults.
wheel.file.migrated: Your wheel settings from launcher 1.2.x now drive the virtual Driving Force Pro. Check the buttons below.
wheel.file.refused: The wheel file had an error the game refuses ({detail}). A copy was kept beside it, and the wheel stays off until you change a setting here.
wheel.file.newer: The wheel file was written by a newer GT4Recomp and is kept as it is. Update the launcher to change it.
wheel.prompt.steer_left: Turn the wheel fully to the left
wheel.prompt.steer_right: Now turn it fully to the right
wheel.game_running: The game is running: close it to change the wheel's controls or test the force.
wheel.wizard.title: Set up {name}
wheel.wizard.intro: The launcher starts from the {family} mapping, then asks for each control: turn the wheel, press each pedal and each button. Every step can be skipped, and every control can be changed later.
wheel.wizard.feet: Keep your feet off the pedals until they are asked for.
wheel.wizard.stopped: Set-up stopped. The controls set so far are kept.
wheel.wizard.done_text: {bound} of {total} controls are set, and the wheel is on in the game. Save the mapping as a preset to keep a copy.
rust.wheel.game_running: The game is running: close it to change the wheel's controls or test the force.
rust.wheel.newer_file: The wheel file was written by a newer GT4Recomp and is kept as it is. Update the launcher to change it.
rust.wheel.could_not_save: The wheel settings could not be saved: {error}
rust.wheel.unknown_template: There is no wheel template named {name}.
setting.armsx2_textures.label: Custom textures
setting.armsx2_textures.help: Load texture packs with the ARMSX2 GS from the folder chosen below (the same packs and the same PCSX2 folder layout as on the PC: the game's serial folder with its replacements folder). Off uses the game's own textures. Your own extra GS lines go into armsx2-gs-extra.ini, beside armsx2-gs.ini in the app's files folder.
setting.armsx2_upscaler.label: Upscaler
setting.armsx2_upscaler.help: FSR1 (AMD) and Snapdragon Super Resolution (Qualcomm) work only on Vulkan: this row appears while Vulkan is chosen. Under OpenGL ES only the normal sharpening (CAS) is used.
vpad.section_help: Shows a controller on the screen while you play on a phone, for when you have no physical controller. Auto shows it only while no controller is connected; Always keeps it on screen; Off never shows it. Adjust the buttons with Edit layout.
vpad.reset_text: The button positions, sizes and opacity go back to the built-in layout. This is saved at once.
vpad.reset_done: The virtual controller is back to its default layout.
vpad.notes: The saved layout could not be used, so the default one is shown. Edit layout saves a new one.
vpad.locked: The layout file was written by a newer GT4Recomp and is kept as it is. Update the launcher to edit it.
vpad.canvas_label: The virtual controller layout. Tab or the D-pad selects a button; the arrows move it.
vpad.no_selection: Tap a button, or press Tab or the D-pad, to change it.
vpad.warn_f7: On the F7 report button: {names}. Move them so the corner stays free.
vpad.discard_text: The changes in this editor are lost; the saved layout stays as it was.
vpad.problem.opacity: the opacity is not between 0 and 100%
vpad.problem.duplicate_id: two buttons have the same name
vpad.problem.type: a button has an unknown type
vpad.problem.binds: a button has an unknown binding
vpad.problem.x: a button is off the screen sideways
vpad.problem.y: a button is off the screen up or down
vpad.problem.size: a button size is out of range
vpad.problem.width: a button width is out of range
vpad.problem.element_opacity: a button opacity is out of range
vpad.problem.deadzone: a stick dead zone is out of range
